items.title: google-deepmind/mujoco
items.contentSnippet:
Multi-Joint dynamics with Contact. A general purpose physics simulator.
https://mujoco.org

  
 
             
 
MuJoCo stands for Multi-Joint dynamics with Contact. It is a general purpose physics engine that aims to facilitate research and development in robotics, biomechanics, graphics and animation, machine learning, and other areas which demand fast and accurate simulation of articulated structures interacting with their environment.
 
This repository is maintained by Google DeepMind.

items.title: Show HN: Crayon, the web's first personalized newspaper (1995), relaunched
items.contentSnippet:
In 1995 I co-built CRAYON (CReAte Your Own Newspaper) - the first personalized news service on the web. 650k people made papers. The Perl CGI site ran, barely, for 31 years. I've now rebuilt it: stories ranked by independent-source count instead of an editor or engagement algorithm, every side of every story on one page. Your 1996 password still works, and every subscriber can open their original paper as a time capsule - dead sources marked "lost to time."
Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator

items.title: Show HN: Caramel: a speech-to-speech conversation model trained only on audio
items.contentSnippet:
I trained a speech-to-speech model last night, inspired by Dessa. I'm calling the model caramel-1. The model learned from recordings of people talking and nothing else, and has never seen a single word of text. The code, the training recipe and the weights are open source.
caramel-1 sounds incredibly human. Most of what caramel-1 says doesn't make sense yet, but the sentences make a little more sense every time I add more data.

items.contentSnippet:
One binary to run and you have a full backend at your fingertips: a database with a REST API, sign-in, realtime, files, server-side hooks and jobs, on SQLite or Postgres. It's MIT licensed.
You can try the demo at https://demo.vaultbase.sh (the login is filled in, and it resets every hour).

items.title: Show HN: PDFMeasure – Measure PDF files in the browser
items.contentSnippet:
Hi HN, sharing a little app I built to measure architectural drawings in the browser. My architects on a remodel had this fancy software to do it, but I was frustrated to not be able to do the same easily.
It does much of what the more complex software does: measure distance, surface areas, perimeters, angles; markup; takeoff (count & run lengths), ...etc. I even built an overlay feature to compare two pages.
